finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF (and local file read): the POST parameter 'feed' is passed directly to file_get_contents(), which accepts http(s)://, ftp://, file://, php:// and other wrappers. The response length is echoed, giving a blind/oracle channel for internal URLs and local files. No auth, scheme/host allowlist, or private-IP blocking.

trace.note: Only checks REQUEST_METHOD === POST and isset($_POST['feed']); no auth
User-controlled value passed to file_get_contents() as URL/path
strlen of fetched body echoed to attacker, confirming reachability and content size

finding.guards_checked: require_admin() is defined but not called on this path. No scheme allowlist, host allowlist, DNS/IP resolution check, or redirect restriction. allow_url_fopen is assumed enabled (PHP default).

verdict.reason: import.php:11-13 passes unauthenticated $_POST['feed'] straight to file_get_contents() and echoes strlen of the result, with no auth or URL/host/scheme validation (require_admin() at line 4 is only called at line 18 for the unrelated set_webhook branch).

finding.claim: Admin-only SSRF: the 'set_webhook' POST parameter is used as the URL for curl_init()/curl_exec() and is requested immediately. No scheme or host validation, so an admin (or an attacker who has a session with is_admin, e.g. via XSS/CSRF since no CSRF token is checked) can make the server request internal services such as cloud metadata or localhost. Lower severity because of the admin gate.

trace.note: Branch entered when set_webhook is present

finding.guards_checked: require_admin() (session is_admin) is enforced. There is no URL scheme/host allowlist, no private-IP blocking, no CSRF protection, and CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS / CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION are not restricted. The response is not returned to the caller (blind SSRF).

verdict.guard_found: require_admin() session is_admin check (import.php:4-9, 18). There is no URL validation, and no CSRF token.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (import.php:17-22), but the sink at import.php:20 is only reachable after require_admin() at import.php:18. An unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker therefore cannot control the URL. The CSRF and XSS routes to an admin session are speculative, and nothing in the code shows them.
